note: FNS 1160.1 requires the QC reviewer to document five elements: type of allowance, household entitlement, source of excluded vendor payments, verification obtained, and explanation of variances. The OLG covers the underlying caseworker-facing policy well: it defines the three SUA types (HCSUA, Non-Heating, Telephone), explains entitlement criteria for each, details verification standards (self-declaration acceptable, lists of acceptable documents if questionable), and provides thorough BEACON procedures for entering SUA data via Yes/No utility questions. The HCSUA page explicitly warns that 'The case record must accurately reflect the utility expenses the household is reporting to pay. Failure to document which utilities a household is responsible for will result in...a Quality Control error.' The OLG also requires narrative annotation for expense changes ('Annotate the Narrative tab explaining the action taken'). However, two gaps exist: (1) Documentation of excluded vendor payments is only addressed in the veterans benefits context (Federal and State Veterans Benefits pages require 'create a detailed narrative identifying the vendor payments made on the veteran's behalf and the verification provided'), with no general SUA-level guidance on documenting other excluded vendor payments; (2) There is no consolidated documentation standard or checklist for SUA determinations — the requirements are distributed across multiple pages (SUA Expense Introduction, HCSUA, Non-Heating SUA, Telephone SUA, Entering SUA Data, SUA Page). The variance explanation requirement is QC-specific and has no direct caseworker equivalent in the OLG, though narrative annotation requirements partially serve this purpose.
